narrative.overview: SentryVision's visual system embodies vigilant calm. The dark canvas is night; the interface is the watch post — alert, composed, never loud. Every element earns its place through function, not decoration. The palette is almost entirely neutral — deep charcoals and muted grays — with a single accent color reserved exclusively for interactive states and system status. When the accent appears, it means something. The aesthetic draws from Linear's instrument-grade precision: dense information hierarchy, hairline separation, monospace data, and controls that feel like machined hardware.
keyCharacteristics: OLED-black canvas with tonal surface layering (no shadows for depth, only border contrast)
Single muted indigo accent used sparingly — rarity is the point
Geist typeface family: geometric sans for chrome, monospace for data
Pill-shaped controls with inset highlights and press-down scale (0.97)
Hairline borders as the primary depth language
Bottom dock navigation with animated sliding indicator
Zero glassmorphism, zero backdrop-blur on cards — solid surfaces only

rules.name: The Restraint Rule
rules.body: The primary accent appears on ≤15% of any screen. When it appears, it means something: an active state, a primary action, or a status indicator. Never use it for decoration, backgrounds, or decorative gradients.

rules.name: The Tonal Surface Rule
rules.body: Depth is communicated through surface color steps, not shadows. Canvas (#050505) → Surface (#0A0A0B) → Raised (#121215) → Control (#1A1A1D).

rules.name: The Data Font Rule
rules.body: All temporal data (timestamps, durations, IDs, percentages) uses Geist Mono with tabular-nums. No exceptions. Monospace is never used for UI chrome.

rules.name: The Tracking Rule
rules.body: Large text gets tighter tracking (-0.02em to -0.04em). Small uppercase labels get wider tracking (0.04em). Body text has zero tracking.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Every surface is flat at rest. Cards never cast shadows. Depth comes from surface color contrast and hairline borders.

rules.name: The Pill Button Rule
rules.body: All primary and secondary action buttons use the pill shape. The pill is the system's signature interactive silhouette.

rules.name: The Concentric Bezel Rule
rules.body: Premium containers use a 1px inset highlight bezel — a machined edge that suggests physical depth without shadows.

dos: Do use the Border Scale (0.06 → 0.10 → 0.16) as the primary depth language.
Do use Geist Mono for all temporal and numeric data. Tabular figures always.
Do use the pill shape for all primary action buttons.
Do use active:scale-[0.97] on every pressable element.
Do use transition duration-150 for state changes. Fast and deliberate.
Do use surface color steps to communicate depth.
Do keep the primary accent under 15% of any screen.
donts: Don't use drop shadows on cards or content containers.
Don't use backdrop-filter: blur() on scrolling content or cards.
Don't use transition-all on buttons or inputs. Specify exact properties.
Don't use ease-in for UI animations.
Don't use the primary accent for decorative backgrounds or gradients.
Don't use 100vh for full-height sections. Always 100dvh.
Don't use generic circular spinners. Skeleton loaders matching content shape.
